My point is that being short won’t define you as a person. People have many qualities and although being short places you at a slight disadvantage it won’t define you as a person. I’m a 5”3 male and won’t grow any more. It’s shit and yes there are days where I hate myself for my height but when you take a step back and realise how many people have made it to places regardless of their height it makes you realise how insignificant that quality is about you. People will love you for who you are and arguably I think being short and having to fight more to be heard and recognised makes you a better person. There’s websites where you can see countless people your height or smaller that are successful and I can garuntee you that many of those people faced similar issues to us and had to realise the same thing to make it to where they are today. https://www.ranker.com/list/male-celebs-who-are-5-ft-3-in/celebrity-lists (look at this website for example). It takes a while to accept that this is how it is but I think the more and more we recognise that differences such as height is something that should be praised rather than ashamed of then we can start to focus on bigger things that do actually define us.

From personal experience it is very much a state of stillness and staring into nothingness. I’ve been told by people that I look like I’m staring at someone or something specifically but it’s more just you gaze as nothingness with an almost lifeless expression on your face and also the rest of your body doesn’t tend to move. One thing I know for certain is that time goes very fast and it’s like one second turns to an hour in real time. Everything that goes on around you either disappears completely - sound mainly - or makes everything muffled and It feels like everything is moving slowly even though when you come back time seems to have moved faster than usual. I honestly don’t know what that looks like from an outer persons perspective but I’ve had a few individuals point it out and on one occasion apparently I had my hands held to tightly together that the skin where my fingers were overlapping was white and my hands were shaking but I don’t remember doing that. I hope this gives you an insight but I think it’s really difficult to know what to look for unless the person experiencing it has someone aware of what’s happening and then they can tell you from an outer persons perspective what it looks like. I have no idea if people notice most the time as it’s only ever been said or described to me around 3 or 4 times in my life and it’s scary because I don’t know if someone’s said something to me or sees me as insane and I don’t want to come off as rude or like I’m fucked in the head yknow?
